name: Galileo Galilei Planetarium
features: Sphere-like concrete form round a 20 m domed projection hall with 360 seats, on its own in Palermo's parks.
note: Argentina has no freedom of panorama but these photos are on Commons. Inaugurated 20 Dec 1966, opened to the public 1968.

name: Puente de la Mujer
features: Swing footbridge: its 102.5 m middle span hangs from a raked 34 m steel mast and turns on one pylon for boats.
note: Category holds 60+ files.

name: Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat
features: Glass-walled gallery under a curved metal roof, set along the Puerto Madero dock.
note: Year from general knowledge (opened 2008); check before publishing.

name: MALBA, Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires
features: Stone-clad blocks and glass volumes round a tall central atrium crossed by escalators.
commons_category: Category:Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires

photos.file: File:Fachada del Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires (MALBA).jpg

note: Facts from general knowledge; confirm architects and year before publishing.

name: Hotel Unique
features: The whole hotel is a 100 m inverted arc, 25 m high, its curved sides dotted with round windows.

photos.file: File:Ruy ohtake, hotel unique, sao paulo brazil april 2006 (698675849).jpg

name: Serra Dourada Stadium
features: Exposed-concrete stadium bowl; look at the structural rhythm and the long access ramps.
note: Wikipedia's works list gives 1973 (design); the stadium opened in 1975. Check which year the site wants.

name: Faro del Comercio
features: A 70 m orange concrete slab on the Macroplaza, with a laser at the top that sweeps the city at night.

photos.file: File:Faro del Comercio, Luis Barragan - panoramio.jpg

note: Height and laser from general knowledge; confirm before publishing.

name: Capilla del Retiro
features: Chapel set down into the ground below a lattice of laminated timber beams and glass, open to the Andes.
note: Features line from general knowledge; confirm.

name: Jesús Soto Museum of Modern Art
features: Low gallery pavilions linked round garden courts, made for Jesús Soto's kinetic art.
commons_category: Category:Jesús Soto Museum of Modern Art

photos.file: File:Jesús Soto Museum of Modern Art facade.jpg

note: Opened 25 Aug 1973 (Commons file of the inauguration).

name: Museo del Oro Quimbaya
features: Brick museum built round open courts and water channels, entered through a sequence of patios.
note: Year and features from general knowledge; confirm.

name: Unilever Offices, Paraguay
features: Office building in exposed brick, an early showcase of Benítez's structural brickwork.
note: Only one file (2586x1830). Check it shows this building; year from general knowledge.

name: Hospital Naval Pedro Mallo
features: Testa's sculptural concrete hospital on the edge of Parque Centenario, often read as a moored ship.
note: Wikipedia lists it among Testa's 1970s works; 1981 completion from general knowledge.

name: National Art Schools (Escuelas Nacionales de Arte)
by: Ricardo Porro, Vittorio Garatti, Roberto Gottardi
features: Five schools of local brick and Catalan tile vaults on a former golf course; Porro's art school is a village of domes.

File:Schools of Modern Dance and Visual Arts, Havana, Cuba LCCN2010638999.tif
File:Schools of Modern Dance and Visual Arts, Havana, Cuba LCCN2010639000.tif

note: Carol M. Highsmith photos (Library of Congress, public domain), 6144x4096. The Garatti ballet file is named 'Divisare copy': its own-work claim may be doubtful.

name: Jaú Bus Station
features: Bus station under one concrete roof carried on columns that branch out round skylights; ramps link the levels.
note: Category has 30+ new files (Sept 2026). Year and features from general knowledge; confirm.

name: La Pampa Civic Centre (Casa de Gobierno)
features: Testa's first big work: a 180 m concrete government front modulated by brise-soleils, on a civic plaza.
note: Photo under the 800px rule only (899x489, 1960s, public domain). Inaugurated 30 Aug 1963; competition win with Dabinovic, Gaido and Rossi. Commons also has 1280px public-domain photos of Testa's Chamber of Deputies next door (Category:Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de La Pampa).

name: Bacardi Bottling Plant
features: Roof of three square groined vaults, each two intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids, 4 cm thick at the edges.

photos.file: File:Planta embotelladora de Bacardí-Instalaciones industriales de Ludwig Mies van der Rohe y Félix Candela.jpg

note: Only one file (1359x919). Its title names both Mies's office and Candela's plant; check it shows the vaults. If not, this is a strong drawing candidate (three hypar groined vaults on a 30 x 90 m plan).

name: Casa no Butantã (Paulo Mendes da Rocha House)
features: One raised concrete floor on just four pillars; closed end walls, long window bands to east and west.
view: Long (east) elevation: the raised concrete box with its roof slab, continuous window band and two of the four pillars, garden level open beneath.
note: Twin houses (his own and his sister's); the drawing shows one. Dates differ: most sources 1964, others 1964-66 or 1967. Commons has one file, File:Paulo Mendes da Rocha - Casa Butantã.JPG (2560x1325, CC BY-SA 4.0), described only as 'view towards the garden of a house by PMR' and filed under 'Architectural elements'; it may be taken from inside. If it clearly shows the outside, use it instead of the drawing.

name: Forma Furniture Showroom
features: A closed prism lifted on two 30 m beams over street parking; one full-width shop window faces the avenue.
view: Street elevation: the long lifted box, its full-width shop-window band near the bottom, the end supports, and the free parking level below.
note: Designed 1987, built 1987-1994 (Wikipedia lists 1987). Sources confirm two prestressed beams of about 30 m, four concrete supports paired at the two ends holding stairs and services, and a shop window about 2 m above the street across the plot's full width. The often-quoted fold-down entrance stair is not confirmed by the sources found, so it is not drawn. Box height and panel lines are not given by sources; the drawing keeps the box plain.

name: Casa Cien
features: Seven storeys of identical square modules: a two-storey base set into the hill and a five-storey studio tower.
view: Side elevation: the three-module, two-storey base partly buried in the hillside, the one-module five-storey tower rising from its centre, and the open roof module.
note: Sources: twelve identical square modules, eleven indoors and one on the roof; base of three modules over two floors, five-storey tower from its centre; poured concrete with chipped, exposed aggregate. Window positions are not described, so none are drawn; the roof module is shown as an open frame.

name: Casa Klotz
features: A white timber box, 6 x 6 x 12 m, nearly closed to the south and opened to the beach with a double-height living room.
view: North (beach) elevation: the symmetrical box with the central double-height glazed living room, two recessed upstairs balconies and the low timber deck.
note: Sources confirm the box size, white-painted boards, symmetrical plan, double-height centre with floor-to-ceiling glazing, two upstairs bedrooms on recessed balconies and a deck 30 cm above ground; the ramped bridge entrance is on the other side and not shown. Exact sizes of the side openings are approximate.

name: Open Chapel of Lomas de Cuernavaca (Palmira Chapel)
by: Félix Candela, with Guillermo Rosell and Manuel Larrosa
features: A single 4 cm hyperbolic-paraboloid saddle that opens 30 m wide at the front and rises to a 21 m point.
view: Front elevation: the open front edge of the saddle shell rising from two ground points to its 21 m tip, with the lower rear edge seen through the opening.
note: Dated 1958-59. Sources give 21 m height (one says 60 ft) and a 30 m front opening; the height of the lower rear edge is not given and is drawn indicatively. No Commons files found under Palmira, Lomas de Cuernavaca or Candela.

name: Club Táchira
features: Thin concrete shell roof, worked out with Torroja from a warped curve and a flat catenary.
note: Only Commons photo is File:Club Táchira.jpg (915x660, CC BY 3.0), but it is a night shot tagged 'Blurred images', so not usable. Sources disagree on the date (1954 study, 1957) and one 2016 paper says Torroja's roof was never built as designed, so the shell's built form can't be drawn with confidence.

name: Salto Bus Terminal
features: Reinforced-brick vaults cantilevered both ways from a single row of slim columns, with no side walls.
note: No Commons files. Sources confirm a double cantilever of ceramic vaults on one row of pillars (about 14 m overhang, 1973-74) but disagree on vault type (free-standing barrel vs Gaussian) and give no count of vaults or bays.

name: Casa Berlingieri
features: A row of parallel brick-vaulted rooms facing the Atlantic: Dieste's first reinforced-brick vault.
note: No Commons files. Sources confirm a series of parallel vaulted spaces facing the sea but not the number of vaults, their proportions or the elevations. Dates differ (1946-47, 1949).

name: Museo de Sitio Julio C. Tello
features: Three low volumes of reddish pozzolan concrete linked by open-air corridors in the Paracas desert.
note: No Commons photo. Sources describe materials and the three linked volumes but not roof shapes or heights.

name: House for the Poem of the Right Angle
features: Black concrete pavilion under one 15 m vault, round a glazed courtyard, with projecting trapezoidal rooflights.
note: No Commons files. Irregular biomorphic form (one curved wall, one inclined column, three rooflights) that can't be drawn accurately from text. Radić won the 2026 Pritzker, so demand may rise.

name: Paraguay and Suipacha Artists' Studios
by: Antoni Bonet, Ricardo Vera Barros, Abel López Chas
features: Corner block of shops and two floors of artists' studios: curved glass, steel frames, two vaulted rooftop studios.
note: No Commons files found. Sources list the elements (undulating ground-floor shop windows, large steel frames, glass block, vertical louvres, two vaulted attics) but not how they sit on the corner facades. Sources differ on Vera Barros's first name.

name: Igreja Espírito Santo do Cerrado
features: A small church built with its community on the edge of Uberlândia, drawing on early circular Christian churches.
note: No Commons files. Sources found don't describe the volumes, so it isn't drawn.

name: Casa Bola
features: An 8 m ferrocement sphere, built by hand over a steel-pipe frame on top of the architect's office and home.
note: No Commons files. The sphere is clear, but sources don't describe the building it sits on, so the whole can't be drawn with confidence. Built 1974-79; opened to the public for the first time in 2026.

name: Praxis (Taller de Arquitectura Agustín Hernández)
features: A concrete 'tree': a central stair trunk carries four polyhedral T-shaped studio modules, reached by a bridge.
note: Only a photo of a model is on Commons (1803x2488). The polyhedral geometry (60-degree edges, modules in tension and compression) is too complex to draw from text alone. Built 1972-75.

name: Massaro Agroindustries
features: Industrial sheds roofed with Dieste's double-curvature (Gaussian) reinforced-brick vaults.
note: No Commons files. Domus confirms double-curvature brick vaults and 1980; no source found gives the number of vaults, spans or any cantilever, so it isn't drawn.

name: Edifício Louveira
features: Two apartment slabs on pilotis facing each other across a shared garden open to the square, linked by a ramp.

photos.file: File:Edifício Louveira, João Batista Vilanova Artigas e Carlos Cascaldi (5877913511).jpg

note: Wikipedia: Louveira Residential Complex, 1946-1949. Commons descriptions confirm two buildings, pilotis, central garden and access ramp. 50+ files.

name: Second Artigas House (Residência Vilanova Artigas II)
features: Artigas's own house of 1949, built before his concrete houses of the São Paulo school.
note: Wikipedia lists 'Artigas House, São Paulo, 1948-1949'. The three concepts are not confirmed by a source; check them before publishing. 17 files on Commons, all 4288x2848 CC BY-SA 4.0 (02 is a front view of the facade).

name: Casa Gerassi
features: A raised house assembled from factory-made precast, prestressed concrete beams, columns and slabs in a few days.
note: Only File:FrontalCasaGerassi.jpg (320x240, public domain) on Commons, too small. Sources confirm precast elements and a raised platform (1989-91) but not the number of columns, heights or openings.

name: Heroico Colegio Militar
features: Military academy campus in Tlalpan whose concrete buildings reinterpret pre-Hispanic forms.
note: Commons category holds only ceremony and cadet photos, none clearly of the buildings. No reachable source described the buildings' forms; architects, year and features are from general knowledge and must be checked.
